answer: In this PoA design, each agent identity is issued only after remote attestation proves an approved TEE enclave measurement, MRENCLAVE, and binds its cryptographic key to that hardware-backed instance. A copied virtual machine may reproduce software, but not the attested secret or measurement on another host; creating another identity therefore requires purchasing additional physical silicon and passing attestation. Whether deployed near a knoll, lagoon, or echo service, duplication remains costly.
